## Published measurements

First-party benchmark data from a bachelor thesis written during an internship
at Advantech in Tokyo, comparing CPU and NPU inference for real-time object
detection on a drone companion computer. Hardware: Advantech ASR-D501, built on
the Qualcomm QCS6490 with an integrated Hexagon NPU. All figures measured by the
author; the full thesis is linked from the site.

YOLOv8n, same model, three targets (frames per second):
- ASR-D501 Hexagon NPU (INT8): 110.3
- ASR-D501 ARM CPU: 1.3
- Raspberry Pi 5 CPU: 1.1

NPU throughput by model, INT8, ASR-D501 (frames per second):
- YOLOv8n 110.3, YOLOv8s 89.9, YOLOv8m 42.6, YOLOv8l 30.8, YOLOv8x 20.3
- YOLOv11n 103.5, YOLOv11s 82.6, YOLOv11m 40.2

Headline findings:
- NPU inference is roughly 85x the throughput of the same board's CPU.
- The NPU build draws about 10% less total board power than the CPU build,
  giving roughly 67x better inference performance per watt.
- Deployment path: PyTorch -> ONNX -> INT8 TensorFlow Lite, plus adapting a
  vendor Yocto GStreamer pipeline to Ubuntu and handling per-sensor camera input.

## Other work

- GeoMeta Map (https://github.com/Holo911/geometa-map-github): an interactive
  world map for learning GeoGuessr country clues. Notes are attached per
  country in Markdown, filed under categories such as bollards, signs, license
  plates and utility poles, and tagged. The map can be recoloured by tag to
  show every country sharing a clue at once, turning individual notes into
  visible patterns. Each country also stores driving side, top-level domain,
  phone prefix, currency and writing system.
- EraseAll (https://github.com/Holo911/EraseAll): an image editor that removes
  people and objects from photographs and inpaints the background. Includes an
  automatic person-detection mode that labels everyone in the frame so unwanted
  subjects can be removed in one click, plus edge-snapping and manual brush
  selection and a clone stamp. Runs entirely offline on a laptop CPU with no
  GPU and no uploading of images.
- Autonomous drone built from scratch: YOLO detection drives yaw commands to the
  flight controller over MAVLink/ROS 2. Demonstrated live at Japan IT Week,
  Tokyo Big Sight.
- Real-time SLAM with RTAB-Map on the same companion computer.
- Penetration testing engagements for two real clients (a secondary school with
  1000+ networked devices, and a pharmacy), findings scored with CVSS and
  presented to management.
- Honeypot and CTF platform with Grafana monitoring; withstood a live attack
  exercise without a breach.
- Hardened C BIOS flashing utility using POSIX fork/execvp with input
  allowlisting, removing the shell-injection surface.
- ROS 2 stop-and-wait navigation behaviour tree for safe operation around people.
